transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we prepare for this afternoon's medication safety review of the new IV anticoagulant protocol, I'd like to hear from each of you before I make my final decision on safeguards. Pharmacy, let's start with you — any operational findings related to stocking, labeling, or dispensing of the medication from the automated cabinets? Lab, nursing education, and IT, I'll be looking for your input as well.

transcript.text: I need to report a significant safety concern. Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. As a safeguard, pharmacy can remove the bedside stock from the automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have an important lab operational finding for the safety review. The anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement is an aPTT test every six hours for patients receiving this protocol. Morgan, this monitoring schedule will need to be factored into any safeguards you put in place this afternoon.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a nursing education finding for the safety review. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Each of these nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before administering the medication. Morgan, this competency gap will need to be addressed as a safeguard before the protocol is used on the night shift.

This alert will warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before the order can be released. Morgan, this can serve as an additional safeguard alongside the measures pharmacy, lab, and nursing education have proposed.

decisions.safety_protocol: Temporary hold on the new IV anticoagulant protocol for adult inpatients until the medication safety review safeguards are fully implemented tonight.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: Remove bedside stock of both 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL concentrations from automated dispensing cabinets; supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes to eliminate concentration selection errors.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: Use aPTT testing every six hours for all patients receiving the anticoagulant protocol, as the anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00.
decisions.nurse_authorization: Require charge-nurse sign-off before any of the 18 nurses who have not completed the anticoagulant administration module may administer the medication on tonight's shift.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority electronic medication-record alert at 16:00 today to warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before order release.

Maintain a temporary hold on the new IV anticoagulant protocol until all four safeguards are confirmed in place before the night shift begins.
